newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit limps to easier close in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit limps to easier close in quiet trade.

text.p: The ringgit limped to an easier close against the dollar in quiet trading Friday, dealers said.
Participants were sidelined ahead of Friday's release of U.S. retail sales and consumer price index data, they said.
Tensions between the U.S. and Iraq also did not shift to a higher gear. "The dollar popped up a bit in the afternoon, but that's about the only movement," said a local bank dealer.
At the 1000 GMT local close, ringgit was at 2.4975/85 per dollar against 2.4986/91 on Thursday.
Dealers said ringgit fundamentals remained sound with strong support from Malaysian exporters at 2.5010/15.

In the interbank market, the overnight rate was kept steady at 6.0 percent. Dealers said market liquidity remained high but that rates were prevented from falling due to worries of a Bank Negara intervention.
